packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-06 - unverified image reading (blind first reader)

Exposure statement: no proposed identification of the work or author was in my context. The overview image-006 shows a library stamp and a pencil shelfmark at the foot ("Fragm. lat. 110"); I note it as visible on the image, and did not use it to identify anything. I did nothing beyond the stated rules (I listed the packet directories only to find the image filenames, and checked that the four PROMPT.md files were identical).

LAYOUT SURVEY (observations)
- Two faces of one damaged parchment fragment: face A = overview image-001 (tiles image-002..005); face B = overview image-006 (tiles image-007..010). Leaf is cut irregularly and was folded (binding reuse: fold lines, sewing thread at lower left of face A, holes).
- Each face: two columns of text, ruled, Gothic book hand, brown ink. Roughly 32-34 lines per column survive.
- Rubrication: red initials (2-line) and red paragraph marks / touched capitals; red underlining of some words (face A col. a line 3 and near mid-column). Face A col. b ends with a red line heading: "De sp(eci)eb(us) timoris · lxxxiij" (number reading uncertain: lxxxiij / lxxxiiij?) - looks like a chapter title with chapter number placed at the end of a chapter (tentative).
- Red marginal letters (single letter, possibly "g"/"d") in the right margin of face A, and a red "au?" mark in the left margin of face B: possibly guide letters or notes (interpretation tentative).
- No running titles visible; no interlinear glosses apart from superscript abbreviation marks.
- Text appears to be continuous prose with embedded citations (Gen., Mt., Io., Aug., Glo., G.) - a compilatory/treatise style text on fear (timor) with numbered kinds (secundus, tercius?, quarta, quinta, sextus). Interpretation, not identification.
- Face A is badly abraded and stained (white mould/abrasion patches across the middle of both columns); face B is much more legible.

SPANS SELECTED
- Face B col. a (image-007 + image-009), almost whole column.
- Face B col. b (image-008 + image-010), whole column.
- Face A col. b lower half (image-005) including closing rubric; face A col. a top lines (image-002) and scattered words in col. a lower (image-004); face A col. b top (image-003).
Remaining largely unread: face A middle of both columns (abrasion), face A col. a lower half beyond scattered words.
Overlaps: image-007/009 overlap by about 6 lines (image-009 lines 1-4 = image-007 lines 17-20); image-008/010 overlap by about 4-5 lines (image-010 lines 1-4 = image-008 lines 16-20); image-002/004 overlap by about 4 lines; image-003/005 overlap by about 4 lines. Repeated lines are noted, not counted twice.

- Face A is severely abraded/mould-damaged; most of the middle of both columns is unreadable at this resolution. Only scattered words there.
- Upper part of face B col. a and col. b lines 4-5 run across a fold and are worn.
- Line numbering is counted per tile from the topmost (partly visible) line, so numbers are approximate where a line is cut at the tile edge.
- Readings marked (?) are uncertain; expansions in parentheses are mine. Biblical-looking phrases were transcribed from the visible letters only, not completed from memory; where letters were missing I left [ ].
- Suggest: raking-light or UV images of face A, and higher-contrast processing of the fold area on face B.
